actions-list.actionItem: The House proceeded with one hour of debate on H.R. 9576.

Rule provides for consideration of H.R. 9576, H.R. 10326, H.J. Res. 210 and H.J. Res. 213. The resolution provides for consideration of H.R. 9576, H.R. 10326, H.J. Res. 210, and H.J. Res. 213 under a closed rule with one hour of debate and one motion to recommit on each measure. The resolution provides for a motion to concur in the Senate amendments to H.R. 5334.
Considered under the provisions of rule H. Res. 1530. H.R. 9576 — "To establish the National Fraud Enforcement Division of the Department of Justice."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7730.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Cline moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 7730 — "To amend title 11, United States Code, to modify certain bankruptcy eligibility requirements, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9191.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Ms. Lee (FL) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 9191 — "To amend chapter 3 of title 36, United States Code, to designate the American mastodon as the national fossil mammal and the Tyrannosaurus rex as the national fossil dinosaur of the United States, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7834.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Ms. Lee (FL) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 7834 — "To limit liability for certain entities storing child sexual abuse material for law enforcement agencies, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9570.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 9570 — "To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 117 West Lovett Street in Charlotte, Michigan, as the "Francis C. Flaherty Post Office Building"."
The title of the measure was amended. Agreed to without objection.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8193.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 8193 — "To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 189 East Main Street in Xenia, Ohio, as the "Gilman 'Gil' Whitney Post Office Building"."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 6006.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 6006 — "To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 401 North Elm Street in Tuskegee, Alabama, as the "Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Post Office"."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7365.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 7365 — "To designate the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 1225 Kempsville Road in Virginia Beach, Virginia, as the "Colonel Edward Shames Post Office Building"."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On agreeing to the resolution Agreed to without objection.
Mr. Comer asked unanimous consent to call up H. Res. 1543 and asked for its immediate consideration.
By direction of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, Mr. Comer called up the resolution to accompany House Report 119-831.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on S. 766.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. S. 766 — "To require an annual report of taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule."

Mr. Massie rose to a point of personal privilege. The Chair announced that it was made aware of the basis for the point of personal privilege and recognized Mr. Massie to proceed for one hour on his point of personal privilege.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9086.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Lawler moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 9086 — "To amend the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to modify and improve that Act."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7890.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Walberg moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 7890 — "To amend the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to exclude certain instructional approaches from comprehensive literacy instruction, to prioritize certain funds to promote the use of evidence-based literacy instruction and supports aligned to the science of reading, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9723.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Walberg moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 9723 — "To establish the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8775.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Walberg moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 8775 — "To amend the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959 to provide that individuals who have been convicted of sex offenses against minors may not serve in certain positions."

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on S. 2403.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Walberg moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. S. 2403 — "To amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to provide a clear definition of adequate consideration for certain closely held stock, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7443.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 7443 — "To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to realign the mission of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7436.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 7436 — "To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to implement a standardized training program for employees of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9394.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 9394 — "To require the Department of Homeland Security to conduct an exercise related to agroterrorism, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9382.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 9382 — "To require the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together applications of family members throughout the NEXUS application process, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 5517.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 5517 — "To amend the Northern Border Security Review Act to require updates to the northern border threat analysis and northern border strategy, and for other purposes."
The title of the measure was amended. Agreed to without objection.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 5109.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 5109 — "To require the Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration of the United States to develop guidelines to improve returning citizens' access to the Transportation Worker Identification Credential program, to assist individuals in custody of Federal, State, and local prisons in pre-applying or preparing applications for Transportation Worker Identification Credential cards, and to assist individuals requesting an appeal or waiver of preliminary determination of ineligibility, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9327.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Van Epps moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 9327 — "To establish in U.S. Customs and Border Protection a pilot program to adopt dogs from local animal shelters to be trained as support dogs, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1342.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Perry moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 1342 — "To prohibit discrimination based on political affiliation in granting disaster assistance."

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9497.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Graves moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 9497 — "To provide for improvements to the rivers and harbors of the United States, to provide for the conservation and development of water and related resources, and for other purposes."
The Speaker announced that votes on suspensions, if ordered, will be postponed until a time to be announced.

At the conclusion of debate on H.R. 5334, the Chair put the question on agreeing to the Senate amendments and by voice vote, announced the ayes had prevailed. Mr. Meeks demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
The previous question was ordered pursuant to the rule.
Pursuant to the provisions of H. Res. 1530, the House proceeded with one hour of debate on motion to agree to the Senate amendments to H.R. 5334.
Mr. McCaul moved that the House agree to the Senate amendments.
Pursuant to the provisions of H. Res. 1530, Mr. McCaul called up the Senate amendments to H.R. 5334.
The House proceeded with one minute speeches which by direction of the Chair, would be limited to 15 per side of the aisle.
The Chair designated Mr. Neal to lead the Members in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.
The Speaker announced approval of the Journal.  Pursuant to clause 1, rule I, the Journal stands approved.
Today's prayer was offered by the House Chaplain, Chaplain Margaret Grun Kibben.
The Speaker designated the Honorable Dusty Johnson to act as Speaker pro tempore for today.
The House convened, starting a new legislative day.
